tasks.short: Recruit students, select applicants, and make admissions recommendations.

steps.what: Plan student recruitment events for the coming term.
Take part in student recruitment at fairs and visits.
Read applications for selection and flag missing items.

loop.input: One application file and the required-item list
loop.output: A list of items that are present or missing, with no recommendation
loop.check: Administrator deletes any line that refuses or ranks the applicant
loop.stop: One pass. An incomplete file is flagged, not decided.
loop.why_not_simpler: Files mix forms and free text, so a fixed screen misses letters

steps.what: Make admissions recommendations to admit, refuse or condition.
Record the approved admissions recommendations in student records.
Send the admission letter from the approved recommendation.

tasks.design: Recruitment dates sit on {CALENDAR}. Each application is read once for missing items, and the administrator makes the admissions recommendation in person. {EMAIL} sends the letter, and {OTHER} stores it, only from that signed recommendation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Letters were typed from memory, and a missing document was found late.
tasks.enabler_now: The item list is stable enough to flag gaps, and a letter can be filled from a signed recommendation.
tasks.still_hard: The recommendation itself, and being at the fair.
tasks.human_edge: Only the administrator recommends admission, refusal or a condition. A missing-item list does not.

ambition.what: Whether an application file is complete, within two working days of arrival

tasks.altitude: Fairs stay in the week. Complete files arrive with gaps marked. The administrator still signs every recommendation, and nothing is sent before that.

reach.task: Make admissions recommendations for a school place
reach.learn: Which gaps can be flagged before a person recommends

evidence.claim: GDPR Article 22 says an admission decision must not rest on automation alone, and the person must be able to contest it.
AI Act Annex III points 3(a) and 3(b) cover admissions. Duties are dated from 2 December 2027.
A letter can be filled from fields a person has already signed. The signature is the decision.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one recruitment season's events, one application through to the letter. Offers of funding are a different task.

Structured fields: event date, required item, present or missing, recommendation (admit, refuse, condition), condition text. Admissions staff file the documents. If a required item has no rule, the file is marked unknown and waits.
Use the calendar and the student-record screens that already exist before any custom selector. {OTHER} here is the institution's student information system.
No score ranks applicants. An incomplete file is not a refusal.
unknowns: Which conditions the letter may state without a further committee.
Who else may sign a recommendation when the administrator is away.
Whether the student-record screen can store the three outcomes without a new field.
research_questions: Does the current letter still get retyped after the recommendation is signed?

incremental.description: Keep the required-item list for application files

approvals.approved_version: student-record entry of the signed recommendation
admission letter generated from the approved recommendation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most files are nonstandard and the fair week is heavy. High: the item list is stable and the letter is a short check. The recommendation and the fair stay. Not a measured saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set course schedules and assign teaching and rooms.

steps.what: Collect course hours, room size and teaching availability.
Build course schedules from declared constraints in the timetable tool.
Meet faculty where teaching assignments still clash.
Accept the course schedules and the room assignments.
Publish teaching assignments and room assignments to staff.

tasks.design: Course hours, room size and teaching availability are stored as constraints. The timetable is built by configuring {LMS} and {CALENDAR}, not by scoring people, and clashes are settled with faculty. Assignments go out only after the administrator accepts that timetable.
tasks.previous_blocker: Schedules were shuffled in a spreadsheet, and a clash surfaced after publication.
tasks.enabler_now: The constraints are declared fields, and a timetable product can be configured to respect them.
tasks.still_hard: The clash conversation, and the call when two good constraints cannot both hold.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator accepts the timetable. A draft that still clashes is not published.

ambition.what: Which rooms are free for a short course in the same week

tasks.altitude: The clash meeting stays. A draft with the broken constraints marked is ready before it. Publishing staff assignments still waits for the administrator, and for consent where the roster rules require it.

reach.task: Assign rooms so the building is used without double booking
reach.learn: Which constraints are declared in advance and which are negotiated

evidence.claim: Zermelo builds school timetables. The digest gives a school count this graph does not use. Postsecondary use is not established.
A timetable that uses declared constraints (availability, room size, course hours) is not rostering staff on behaviour or traits under AI Act Annex III 4(a) or 4(b).
WOR article 27: in the Netherlands a roster of staff needs works council consent. Other countries differ.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one term's course schedules, teaching assignments and room assignments. Exam timetables and hiring are out of scope.
Structured fields: course id, contact hours, room capacity, staff availability, clash id. Faculty submit availability. A constraint with no owner is left blank.
Try the native timetable configuration first. If it cannot hold those constraints, stop and schedule by hand. Do not add a custom solver in this task.
A school timetable product is not assumed to fit a university. Staff assignments are not published from traits or performance scores.
In the Netherlands, works-council consent for the roster is obtained before publication. That consent sits outside the timetable screen.
unknowns: Whether the current timetable tool can store room capacity and staff availability without a workaround.
Which assignments the works council must see before publication.
Who may accept a timetable when the administrator is the person who also teaches.
research_questions: Can the installed timetable tool hold a constraint it was not sold for, or does the team still finish in a spreadsheet?

incremental.description: Maintain room, course-hour and availability constraints, and the works-council note

approvals.approved_version: timetable the administrator accepted after the clash meeting
published teaching and room assignments from the accepted timetable

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: constraints arrive late and the clash meeting rebuilds the week. High: constraints are complete and the meeting only clears a short list. The meeting and the acceptance stay. Not a measured saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Prepare course materials for courses in the department.

loop.input: The course outline and the administrator's source notes
loop.output: Draft materials that add nothing beyond those notes
loop.check: Administrator removes any claim, date or reading that is not in the notes
loop.stop: One pass. A section with no source is left as a heading.
loop.why_not_simpler: The outline is prose, not a form with fixed cells

steps.what: Teach courses in the department classroom.
Answer questions students raise after the class.

tasks.design: Course materials are drafted in {LMS} from the outline and released only after the administrator checks them. The class, and the questions after it, stay with the administrator in the room.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials were rebuilt the night before, and the class could not be handed to a screen.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can start from an outline the administrator already wrote.
tasks.still_hard: Teaching the session, and answering what the room actually asks.
tasks.human_edge: Students are taught by the administrator. A draft pack is not the class.
tasks.altitude: The week is still the classroom. Materials are checked rather than rewritten from a blank page. Who teaches does not change.

reach.role: Education and Childcare Administrators, Preschool and Daycare
reach.task: Teach or lead a session with the children present
reach.learn: What can be prepared the day before, and what only happens in the room

evidence.claim: Teaching a course is presence in the room. A prepared pack does not deliver the session.
Materials handed to students are a publication of the institution and need a person to check them first.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: materials, the taught session, and questions immediately after it. Assessment design is a different task.
Structured fields: course id, outline section, source note id. The administrator supplies the notes. A heading with no note is left blank.
Use the learning system already used for the course page before a separate authoring tool.
unknowns: Which sessions the administrator must teach in person.
Whether a colleague may reuse the checked materials.
research_questions: Are the current materials a controlled outline or a folder of old slides?

incremental.description: Refresh the course outline before the term opens

approvals.approved_version: course materials the administrator checked before class

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the outline changes and the class runs long. High: the outline is stable and only the check remains. Teaching stays. Not a measured saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review misconduct reports, decide discipline, and counsel students.

steps.what: Review misconduct reports and pull the stated facts.

loop.output: Facts the report itself states, each tied to a line
loop.check: Administrator deletes any fact that is not in the report
loop.stop: One pass. A gap is marked unknown.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reports are free text, not a fixed incident form

steps.what: Check the report against the disciplinary procedure.
Hear the student named in the misconduct reports.
Decide the disciplinary action, or that none applies.
Counsel students on the report and the decision.
File the disciplinary action on the student record.

tasks.design: Misconduct reports are read for the facts they state, then checked against the written procedure in {DOCS}. The hearing, the disciplinary decision and the counselling stay with the administrator. {OTHER} records the decision only after it is signed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports sat in a mailbox, and the procedure was a PDF nobody opened beside the file.
tasks.enabler_now: A report can be forwarded to a named person, and a procedure check can mark which clauses the facts touch.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing the student, choosing the action, and counselling them.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator decides and counsels. A forwarded report is not a sanction.
tasks.altitude: Hearings and counselling still fill this work. The file arrives with facts and clause marks. The sanction is unchanged as a personal decision.

reach.task: Review a conduct report and speak with the person concerned
reach.learn: Which facts can be listed before the conversation, and which must wait for it

evidence.claim: Zenya keeps a protocol library and forwards an incident report to the person in charge. It does not choose a sanction. A care-home reporting volume is not this job.
The disciplinary action and the counselling are judgements about a student and stay with the administrator.
GDPR Article 22 is stated for scholarship, admission and staff decisions. A sanction is the same kind of decision about a person and is not left to automation.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one misconduct report through hearing, decision, counselling and the record. Appeals to a committee are out of scope.
Structured fields: report id, fact line, procedure clause, decision, counsel date. The reporter files the report. A fact not in the report is not added.
Use the document store and the student-record screen before a separate case tool. {OTHER} is the institution's student information system.
The procedure check does not select the sanction. If the procedure does not cover the facts, the match says unknown.
unknowns: Which reports the administrator must hear in person.
Who may see the decision on the student record.
Whether counselling notes are stored or only the decision.
research_questions: Is the disciplinary procedure a controlled text or a scanned booklet?

incremental.description: Keep the disciplinary procedure text current

approvals.approved_version: disciplinary decision the administrator made after the hearing
student-record entry of that disciplinary decision

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the report is contested and the hearing takes longer. High: facts are clear and the procedure names the range. The hearing, the decision and the counselling stay. Not a measured saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Fairs, the classroom and hearings still take the week. Application gaps, a clash list and a checked course pack are ready first. The administrator still signs every admissions recommendation, every timetable and every disciplinary decision.
reach: Kindergarten through secondary administrators can reuse a missing-item check, not the admissions recommendation
Lodging managers can see a room clash before anyone publishes an assignment
skills_to_grow: Signing a recommendation only after the file's gaps are known
Holding publication while a teaching clash is still unresolved
Separating facts in a misconduct report from the sanction
role.ambitious_version: No admission letter, published teaching assignment or disciplinary record exists without the administrator's signed decision on that case.
